column1: # An id, a name, the names they also go by, what kind of person they are, and
# the day they first appear. NOTHING ELSE.
# *** WHY STATUS AND CONDITION ARE NOT COLUMNS HERE ***
# They are EVENTS WITH DATES and they belong in a log. "Cuddy is frail" is not a
# property of Cuddy; it is something that became true on day 76 and was rolled
# for. "Ancel departed" happened after day 35. Filing that kind of thing as a
# property is exactly how `npcs.md` came to say of Ancel:
#     "Unanswered. He will not sit in the square forever."
# -- which was true for two days, was answered completely on day 34, and was
# still being quoted as live on DAY 77. FORTY-THREE DAYS.
# So: identity here, because identity is stable and makes a safe key. Everything
# that CHANGES goes to campaign/interactions.tsv, campaign/loops.tsv or
# campaign/availability.tsv, where it carries a day.
# kind: pc | henchman | npc | hireling | offstage | dead
#   offstage = named and not yet met. They are real and they are referred to.
#   dead     = still needs a row; the dead are talked about more than the living.
# `aliases` is semicolon-separated and exists so that "Rell's brother" and
# "Gyll" resolve to one person -- nobody in this hundred used his name for two
# years, and the file used both.

Ex-bandit. Cleric since day 39: may not use edged weapons, AC 6 on DEX 4. Cuddy taught her the dwarf's words on day 76

Bern's partner. Thief since day 39. CON 3 -- three raises at most. The lantern and the fuel are her duty, and she asked for it || *** HER AGE IS NOT ESTABLISHED AND MUST NOT BE INVENTED. *** The DM made her thirteen on day 84 by reading CON 3 as frailty and frailty as youth, and built a scene on it. She is BERN'S PARTNER and Bern is ~30. CON IS A CONSTITUTION SCORE.
Cloth and wool trader; FACTOR of the hundred since day 32. The party's money lives with her. Refused them twice before coming round on day 12 "from watching"
Book and curio dealer. Fences the salvage at full value and advised against a city sale AGAINST HIS OWN INTEREST on day 16
~50. Reeve of the north hundred; answers to Sir Aymer and is frightened of him -- Wend's word, and he does not deny it
Carter, ~50. Robbed by Hask's crew; the party bought him a mule. WANTS A RUN and has asked once, on day 40, saying he would not ask twice
Joiner, ~30. Robbed of 6 gp and his kit. Ista's partner. Will not go near the caves and is ashamed of it. The loom is to be his
Carrier. Wethersby to Marchford and back, three days each way, EVERY FORTNIGHT. Told the market about the patrol unprompted and named the party
Nine years on Rell's ground. Runs the barn and the basecamp; has his authority in writing. Built the spring and the lean-to nobody asked for
Ex-bandit, broken leg, will not limp. Keeps the store tally with a nine-year-old holding the pen -- the most accurate document in Wethersby. Cannot read and asked to learn
Ex-bandit. Works Bern's bench, which satisfies Ottir's condition for him indefinitely
Dairywoman off Ferd's old holding, two children. NINE YEARS ON RELL'S GROUND AND SHE CAN GRADE WOOL -- and knows whose is worth buying. Nobody had ever asked her a question about wool
Nan's boy, NINE. Holds the pen for Sarn's tally and now for the wool prices
Rides. Carried the letter to Wace; 3 s.p. a day and the hack, priced by Wend unasked

Flax DRESSER, not a labourer, and says so. A year early for the trade he has. Wend: "don't find him a shovel" || *** THE FLAX SEED ON WEND'S SOUTHERN LIST IS DILL'S PROPOSAL. *** sessions/day-076.md: "Dill's proposal came to her and she has been chewing it... seed is not a crop." A DRESSER who will not work ground is the man who saw the ground could be worked -- and Gyll's four-and-a-bit acres follow from it. The DM said on day 87 that the field was not his finding; it was. || WEND'S "DON'T FIND HIM A SHOVEL" IS ABOUT FARM LABOUR, NOT ABOUT HIS OWN TRADE. Retting, breaking, scutching and heckling are A DRESSER'S WORK and doing them is not being made a labourer. The DM conflated the two on day 88 and the player corrected it.
Minds the beasts. Cannot read and says so as a disqualification, asking for nothing
The innkeeper. Named the SD cask off the bung without tapping it -- strong stock ale, thirty years and not turned
Bonesetter. Set Sarn's leg at midnight and did not ask who he was
Offered Halm 9 gp for his cart. Did not get it
Named Nan to Dave on the road, and Dave said "then bring her"
Took a rope through both palms on the barrel descent -- rope burn, NO hp damage
Nine years beside Coll on Rell's ground. Walked in on the fifth day
Mother of Tibb. At Lyde's learning the loom; better than her son at everything about it except speed
Meg's GROWN SON, not a child -- the DM wrote "two families" once and was corrected
Nearer sixty than fifty. Carries water; cannot lift a fleece
ALMONER, keeps the chapel outside the wall. A cleric of the 3rd level. Read a chest for ten nights by candle at his own expense. FRAIL as of day 76 -- the wet in his chest, seventy-odd, November
Sir Aymer's steward, ~55. Reads for a living, trusts paper more than people, and ASSUMES THE WORST WHEN NOTHING IS PUT IN FRONT OF HIM. Writes down what you say while you are saying it
Usher of the hall, ~40. Answers for how the hall looks and what is in it. Knows wood. CANNOT SPEND A SHILLING AND REFERS UPWARD -- which is why Ottir struck him off the roof question
The lord. Not distant -- he simply does not come. Ottir sees him twice a year and will not ask him for anything
Sir Aymer's, and good at it. Hostile at 25 to eight armed strangers unannounced, then 69 once Dave put his hands up
64. The biggest flock in the hundred and a stone barn with two years of fleece in it. Bought up Rell's ewes cheap rather than watch good ones go for nothing
16, Marrow's son. Knows that flock and that hill better than anyone alive. His father had never once asked him what he wanted
Took Rell's land and turned off half the hands with nothing written down. Made restitution in the square on day 35, selling the grey mare to cover it. FOUR AND A BIT ACRES that would grow flax
Landowner east of the farms; died in the spring. Gave Coll eleven years
Holder. Turned off three at Michaelmas. Nan's word: his wool is honest
Flax. Said no to Dill honestly and said why. The party paid for his barn, seed and winter at his gate
Spinner. Sold her own house to come. Eight miles cross-country from Fenn's -- a couple of hours, not a day
Handed Dill his own hackles over on day 71
Promised a crock a fortnight before, honoured unasked

Small trader east of Marchford; one cart and two hired men he can barely afford. Came north on a rumour TO BUY. Named four buyers who did not know Wethersby existed, on a penny in the pound for three years. RETURNS IN SPRING WITH A PURSE
Carrier, one of the men Osk hands off to. Answered Osk's own day-6 question flat: "Ludbury. That's the whole mystery"
Drover, met on the last stretch into Draycot
The weaver. Will not move. Takes apprentices on his own terms and holds to them exactly
Dyer. Named the vial as REALGAR in his own yard with nobody exposed, for nothing -- and thirty years of telling people what is in a jar has never once been costed
Priest at Marchford and A CLERIC OF THE 5th LEVEL, so he CAN make holy water -- and Marchford has no font. "I can make it. I have never made it"
Mercer, blue shutters. Buys to sell on, which is why he bought a complete Ludbury lot in October
Bought the realgar for 35 gp
Came up every summer for twelve years with money and two carts and bought the district's clip standing. Came late two summers back, then not at all

The fifth of the road crew. Died underground three days before the party met them. HASK HAS NEVER SAID HOW AND THE PARTY HAS NEVER ASKED -- and a DM summary once got the direction backwards. How he died is DM-side

column7: NO NAME, NO RANK, NO DATE. Cuddy's house did not write to ask questions; it wrote to say a man is coming. Loop L017

Magic-user, RETAINED BY THE CHURCH at Ludbury and takes no outside work -- a standing arrangement, not a refusal. First contact day 86, reaction 33 (uncertain) leaning POSITIVE on 86. Answered fully, for nothing, and that is all he can do

A SAGE AT WRAYE, named by Neot on day 91 and NEVER MET. Neot has him only by repute -- a name and a place, no introduction and no advice on approach (d6=3). Said to have the keeping of the books, or near it. DMG p.32 puts sages in large towns and cities, in or near libraries and schools, which is WHY Neot said Wraye on day 86 without being able to say who

*** MET IN THE ENTRANCE CORRIDOR OF QUASQUETON ON DAY 95 AT REACTION 100 -- the highest UNMODIFIED reaction in the campaign. *** Big bare-armed fighting man, hand axe, hard-soled boots, no shield, human. B1 wandering table, level 1, entry 6: a berserker. KNOWS THE PARTY BY DISTRICT REPUTATION (d6=4) -- the licence out of Sir Aymer,s hall, the wool, Ottir,s surety on nine strangers, and nine people who keep walking into a haunted crag and keep walking out. WANTS TO GO ALONG AND WILL NOT TAKE PAY (d6=4), which is a third case the gifts/work finding does not cover. HAS A COMPANION STILL INSIDE THE DUNGEON and said so unprompted. His boots are two of the hard-soled prints in the threshold dust the party has been puzzling over since day 78

BRAND COMPANION. Met day 95 sitting in the MAGIC-MOUTH CORRIDOR with a dying torch, after forty minutes of being too stubborn to walk out and admit a wall had frightened him. REACTION 92, friendly. Shorter and thicker than Brand, dark beard, a mail shirt mended three times, a long knife. SAYS ALMOST NOTHING AND MISSES NOTHING -- asked Tristle out of nowhere how an elf came to have the gnomes tongue and listened to the whole answer. Heard the party honest account of Torsat and Dellie each laid up a week, and answered it with arithmetic: "two of you, for a week, off a kobold. There is two of us." Then picked up one end of the seventy feet of chain and said I WILL CARRY -- committing to more than Dave had offered (d6=5)
